{
  "thinking": "The table is empty and the clock is running. A fish side-on has a clean outline and an obvious tail, so I'll take the pad, sketch it, and get everyone building from it.",
  "say": "Right, let's do a fish! Simple outline, tail at the far end. I've sketched it on the pad: the run starts at the nose, goes along the top and bottom, then splits into the tail. Shout if you want the tail bigger.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 8,
  "point": [8, 10],
  "pad": "take",
  "sketch_clear": true,
  "sketch": [
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[8, 10], [12, 7.5], [18, 7], [22, 8.5], [24, 10]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[8, 10], [12, 12.5], [18, 13], [22, 11.5], [24, 10]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[24, 10], [26, 7], [28, 6]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[24, 10], [26, 13], [28, 14]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[24, 10], [27, 10]]},
    {"type": "label", "x": 10, "y": 9.2, "text": "eye"}
  ],
  "do": "continue",
  "notes": "Animal: fish, facing left. Stroke 1 = top body curve from START at the nose (8,10) to the tail base (24,10). Stroke 2 = bottom body curve, same direction. Strokes 3 and 4 = tail fin arms branching from the tail base. Stroke 5 = tail centre notch. I hold the pad. Plan: trace stroke 1 first so the start line goes out, then 2, then the tail strokes. Mark START on the pad at the nose."
